title: The Shell Commander
story: Beyond the browser, the Shell Commander issues orders to the operating system itself. cy.exec() runs shell commands during test execution — seeding databases, clearing caches, running scripts.
objective: Use cy.exec() to run a shell command and inspect its output.
hints: cy.exec('command') runs a shell command and yields { code, stdout, stderr }
Assert on the exit code: .its('code').should('eq', 0)
cy.exec() runs in the project root by default

title: The Shell Commander — checks exit code
story: A command that exits with code 0 succeeded. The Shell Commander always verifies the exit code before trusting the result.
objective: Assert that cy.exec() returns exit code 0.
hints: cy.exec() yields { code, stdout, stderr }
.its('code').should('eq', 0) asserts success
Non-zero exit codes indicate failure — Cypress will fail the test by default unless failOnNonZeroExit: false

title: The Shell Commander — ignores non-zero exit
story: Some commands intentionally exit with a non-zero code. The Shell Commander uses failOnNonZeroExit to suppress the failure when needed.
objective: Run cy.exec() with failOnNonZeroExit: false to allow non-zero exit codes.
hints: cy.exec(cmd, { failOnNonZeroExit: false }) allows non-zero exits
You can still assert on .its('code') to know the actual code
Useful when running lint checks that return 1 when issues are found

title: The Shell Commander — reads stderr output
story: Error output flows through stderr. The Shell Commander reads it just as easily as stdout.
objective: Run cy.exec() and inspect the stderr output.
hints: cy.exec() yields { code, stdout, stderr }
.its('stderr') accesses error output
Both stdout and stderr are strings — use .should('contain', ...)

title: The Shell Commander — runs a Node script
story: Node.js scripts can be executed directly. The Shell Commander uses cy.exec() to run a one-liner Node script and validate its output.
objective: Use cy.exec() to run a Node.js script via the command line.
hints: cy.exec('node -e "console.log(42)"') runs inline Node code
The output appears in stdout
Useful for seeding test data or resetting state

title: The Scroll Reader
story: Ancient knowledge is stored in files. The Scroll Reader uses cy.readFile() to retrieve that knowledge during tests — reading fixtures, configs, and generated outputs.
objective: Use cy.readFile() to read a file and assert on its contents.
hints: cy.readFile('path/to/file') yields the file contents as a string
Add encoding as second arg: cy.readFile('file.txt', 'utf8')
cy.readFile() retries until the file exists — useful after cy.exec()

title: The Scroll Reader — asserts on JSON contents
story: JSON files yield parsed objects. The Scroll Reader drills into nested properties using .its().
objective: Read a JSON file and assert on a nested property.
hints: cy.readFile() auto-parses JSON files into objects
.its('key') accesses a property of the yielded object
Chain .should('eq', value) after .its() to assert the value

title: The Scroll Reader — reads file written by exec
story: First the Shell Commander writes a file, then the Scroll Reader reads it. A classic pattern for passing data between cy.exec() and cy.readFile().
objective: Write a file with cy.exec() then read it back with cy.readFile().
hints: cy.exec('echo "hello" > /tmp/test.txt') writes a file
cy.readFile('/tmp/test.txt') reads it back
cy.readFile() retries automatically — no need for cy.wait()

title: The Scroll Reader — retries until file exists
story: cy.readFile() retries automatically. The Scroll Reader waits patiently for a file to appear — no cy.wait() needed.
objective: Demonstrate cy.readFile() retry behaviour with a timeout option.
hints: cy.readFile(path, { timeout: 10000 }) retries for up to 10 seconds
Combine with cy.exec() that generates the file asynchronously
This avoids fragile cy.wait(N) patterns

title: The Scroll Reader — reads text encoding
story: Binary files and plain text need different encodings. The Scroll Reader specifies the encoding to get the right representation.
objective: Use cy.readFile() with an explicit encoding like utf8 or base64.
hints: cy.readFile(path, 'utf8') returns a plain string
cy.readFile(path, 'base64') returns base64-encoded content
Default encoding is utf8 for text files

title: The Scroll Scribe
story: The Scroll Scribe inscribes test results and data into files using cy.writeFile(). Test outputs become readable records for future reference.
objective: Use cy.writeFile() to write data to a file during a test.
hints: cy.writeFile(path, contents) writes a file
Contents can be a string, object (written as JSON), or Buffer
cy.writeFile() creates parent directories automatically

title: The Scroll Scribe — writes JSON
story: Objects are automatically serialised to JSON. The Scribe stores structured data for later retrieval.
objective: Write a JavaScript object to a file as JSON using cy.writeFile().
hints: cy.writeFile(path, { key: value }) writes prettified JSON
cy.readFile() will auto-parse it back to an object
Useful for storing test-generated IDs for later tests

title: The Scroll Scribe — appends to a file
story: The Scribe can append lines without erasing previous inscriptions. The flag option controls write vs append mode.
objective: Use cy.writeFile() with the flag option to append to an existing file.
hints: cy.writeFile(path, content, { flag: 'a+' }) appends
Default flag is 'w' — overwrites the file
Useful for accumulating log output across multiple tests

title: The Scroll Scribe — writes and re-reads between tests
story: Data written in one test can be read back in another. The Scribe uses beforeEach and cy.readFile() to share state without brittle globals.
objective: Write a file in one test and read it back in a subsequent test.
hints: cy.writeFile in beforeEach is a good pattern for shared test data
Avoid using JavaScript variables across tests — prefer cy.readFile()
cy.writeFile is synchronous from Cypress's perspective — it completes before the next command

title: The Scroll Scribe — overwrites fixture file
story: Test fixtures sometimes need resetting. The Scribe overwrites them cleanly before each run.
objective: Use cy.writeFile() to reset a fixture before a test runs.
hints: cy.writeFile('cypress/fixtures/data.json', { ... }) overwrites the fixture
Do this in beforeEach to ensure a clean state
cy.fixture() will then read the freshly written version

title: The Environment Oracle
story: Test configuration varies by environment. The Environment Oracle reads from Cypress.env() to keep credentials, URLs, and flags out of test code.
objective: Use Cypress.env() to read an environment variable inside a test.
hints: Cypress.env('KEY') reads a variable set in cypress.config.js env block
You can also set env vars via CLI: --env KEY=value
Cypress.env() returns all env vars as an object when called with no arguments

title: The Environment Oracle — reads a specific key
story: Each variable has a name. The Oracle reads a specific key and uses it in the test logic.
objective: Read a specific Cypress env key and use its value.
hints: Cypress.env('KEY') returns the value for that key, or undefined if not set
You can set a default: const val = Cypress.env('KEY') || 'default'
Avoid hardcoding secrets — use Cypress.env() instead

title: The Environment Oracle — sets an env variable at runtime
story: The Oracle can inscribe new variables during the test run. Cypress.env(key, value) sets a variable for the remainder of the spec.
objective: Set a Cypress env variable at runtime and read it back.
hints: Cypress.env('KEY', value) sets the variable for the current spec
Changes do not persist beyond the current spec file
Useful for sharing state between tests without global variables

title: The Environment Oracle — uses env in cy.visit()
story: Base URLs from environment variables keep tests portable. The Oracle constructs the full URL from Cypress.env() before navigating.
objective: Construct a cy.visit() URL using a value from Cypress.env().
hints: Cypress.config('baseUrl') reads the configured base URL
Combine Cypress.env() values to build dynamic paths
This pattern makes tests portable across staging/production

title: The Environment Oracle — Cypress.config()
story: Beyond env vars, the Oracle reads Cypress configuration values at runtime. Cypress.config() exposes timeout, baseUrl, viewportWidth and more.
objective: Use Cypress.config() to read a configuration value at runtime.
hints: Cypress.config('defaultCommandTimeout') returns the default timeout in ms
Cypress.config('viewportWidth') returns current viewport width
Cypress.config('baseUrl') returns the configured base URL

title: The Great Purge
story: Between tests, stale cookies and storage can leak state. The Great Purge uses clearAllCookies, clearAllLocalStorage, and clearAllSessionStorage to wipe the slate clean.
objective: Use cy.clearAllCookies() to remove all cookies.
hints: cy.clearAllCookies() removes all cookies for all domains
Cypress already clears cookies between tests by default
Use explicitly when you need to clear mid-test
explanation:
Cookie/storage cleanup commands:

```
cy.clearAllCookies();          // clears all cookies
cy.clearAllLocalStorage();     // clears all origins' localStorage
cy.clearAllSessionStorage();   // clears all origins' sessionStorage
cy.getAllLocalStorage().then(data => { expect(data).to.deep.equal({}); });
```

Typically used in `beforeEach` to ensure a clean state between tests.

title: The Great Purge — clears all localStorage
story: localStorage persists between page loads. The Purge sweeps it away with cy.clearAllLocalStorage().
objective: Use cy.clearAllLocalStorage() to remove all localStorage entries.
hints: cy.clearAllLocalStorage() clears localStorage for all origins
cy.getAllLocalStorage() returns an object of all local storage by origin
Cypress clears localStorage between tests by default
explanation:
Cookie/storage cleanup commands:

```
cy.clearAllCookies();          // clears all cookies
cy.clearAllLocalStorage();     // clears all origins' localStorage
cy.clearAllSessionStorage();   // clears all origins' sessionStorage
cy.getAllLocalStorage().then(data => { expect(data).to.deep.equal({}); });
```

Typically used in `beforeEach` to ensure a clean state between tests.

title: The Great Purge — clears all sessionStorage
story: sessionStorage lasts for the tab session. The Purge eliminates it with cy.clearAllSessionStorage().
objective: Use cy.clearAllSessionStorage() to remove all sessionStorage entries.
hints: cy.clearAllSessionStorage() clears sessionStorage for all origins
cy.getAllSessionStorage() returns current sessionStorage contents
sessionStorage is cleared when the tab closes — but Cypress keeps the page open
explanation:
Cookie/storage cleanup commands:

```
cy.clearAllCookies();          // clears all cookies
cy.clearAllLocalStorage();     // clears all origins' localStorage
cy.clearAllSessionStorage();   // clears all origins' sessionStorage
cy.getAllLocalStorage().then(data => { expect(data).to.deep.equal({}); });
```

Typically used in `beforeEach` to ensure a clean state between tests.

title: The Great Purge — reads all localStorage with getAllLocalStorage
story: Before purging, the Archivist inventories all stored data using cy.getAllLocalStorage().
objective: Use cy.getAllLocalStorage() to inspect all localStorage values.
hints: cy.getAllLocalStorage() yields { origin: { key: value } }
The result is keyed by origin URL
Useful for assertions before and after a purge
explanation:
Cookie/storage cleanup commands:

```
cy.clearAllCookies();          // clears all cookies
cy.clearAllLocalStorage();     // clears all origins' localStorage
cy.clearAllSessionStorage();   // clears all origins' sessionStorage
cy.getAllLocalStorage().then(data => { expect(data).to.deep.equal({}); });
```

Typically used in `beforeEach` to ensure a clean state between tests.

title: The Great Purge — full storage reset in beforeEach
story: The cleanest tests start with a completely empty state. The Purge runs in beforeEach to guarantee isolation.
objective: Clear all cookies, localStorage and sessionStorage in beforeEach.
hints: Chain all three clear commands in beforeEach for total isolation
This pattern prevents test pollution from any source
Cypress default test isolation only handles cookies — do localStorage manually if needed

Cookie/storage cleanup commands:

```

title: The Annotation Scribe
story: Tests tell stories. The Annotation Scribe uses cy.log() to add readable messages to the Cypress command log — marking key steps without affecting test execution.
objective: Use cy.log() to add a custom message to the Cypress command log.
hints: cy.log('message') adds a blue annotation in the command log
cy.log() does not affect test pass/fail status
Use template literals for dynamic messages: cy.log(`User: ${name}`)

title: The Annotation Scribe — logs variable values
story: Inspecting values mid-test is powerful. The Scribe logs them with template literals.
objective: Use cy.log() to output a dynamic value during the test.
hints: cy.log(`Value: ${someVar}`) logs the current value
cy.log() inside .then() gives you access to the subject
This is more visible than console.log during test runs

title: The Annotation Scribe — groups log messages
story: Complex tests benefit from section markers. The Scribe uses cy.log() to separate phases: setup, action, assertion.
objective: Use cy.log() as section headers to structure a multi-step test.
hints: Use cy.log() before each phase: setup, act, assert
It creates a readable narrative in the Cypress time-travel log
No performance cost — cy.log() is synchronous and instant

title: The Annotation Scribe — logs inside each iteration
story: When iterating with .each(), the Scribe logs each item to track progress through the loop.
objective: Use cy.log() inside a .each() loop to output the current item.
hints: cy.log() inside .each() logs per iteration
Combine with the index parameter to show progress
cy.log() yields null — chain cy.wrap() if you need to continue a chain after it

title: The Annotation Scribe — logs with multiple args
story: cy.log() accepts multiple arguments separated by spaces. The Scribe uses this to log labels alongside values.
objective: Call cy.log() with multiple arguments.
hints: cy.log('label', value) joins both with a space in the log
You can pass objects — they are serialized with JSON.stringify
Unlike console.log, cy.log appears in the Cypress UI timeline

title: The Debug Sentinel
story: When a test fails unexpectedly, the Debug Sentinel halts execution mid-stream. cy.pause() freezes time so you can inspect the DOM manually.
objective: Understand cy.pause() — place it in a test to pause execution interactively.
hints: cy.pause() stops test execution and shows a Resume button in the runner
Only useful in open (interactive) mode — has no effect in headless runs
Remove cy.pause() before committing — it will hang CI

title: The Debug Sentinel — cy.debug() logs the subject
story: .debug() prints the current subject to the browser console. The Sentinel uses it to inspect what a command yields before asserting.
objective: Chain .debug() on a command to log its subject to the console.
hints: .debug() logs the current subject to the console and yields it unchanged
It is a pass-through — chaining after it works normally
Unlike cy.pause(), .debug() does not halt execution

title: The Debug Sentinel — cy.debug() on a value
story: The Sentinel inspects plain values, not just DOM elements. .debug() works anywhere in the chain.
objective: Use cy.debug() on a non-DOM value like a string or number.
hints: cy.wrap(value).debug() logs the wrapped value
.debug() yields the subject unchanged so you can continue asserting
Check the browser console (F12) to see the debug output

title: The Debug Sentinel — uses cy.then for manual inspection
story: When automated debugging is not enough, the Sentinel uses .then() to run arbitrary code — console.log, debugger, or custom logic.
objective: Use .then() as a manual debugging point inside a test.
hints: .then(subject => { console.log(subject) }) lets you inspect anything
The debugger statement inside .then() triggers browser devtools
.then() is synchronous within the Cypress command queue

title: The Debug Sentinel — using Cypress.log for custom events
story: Advanced sentinels create custom log entries with Cypress.log(). This lets plugins and custom commands appear in the timeline.
objective: Create a custom Cypress log entry using Cypress.log().
hints: Cypress.log({ name, message }) creates a custom timeline entry
Useful inside custom commands to make them visible in the runner
Different from cy.log() — this is the low-level API

title: The Browser Oracle
story: Tests run on Chrome, Firefox, Edge — each with subtle differences. The Browser Oracle uses Cypress.isBrowser() and Cypress.browser to adapt behaviour at runtime.
objective: Use Cypress.browser to read the current browser name and version.
hints: Cypress.browser.name returns 'chrome', 'firefox', 'electron', etc.
Cypress.browser.version returns the browser version string
Cypress.browser.isHeadless is true when running headlessly

title: The Browser Oracle — isBrowser() for conditional logic
story: Some features only work in specific browsers. The Oracle uses Cypress.isBrowser() to skip or adjust tests conditionally.
objective: Use Cypress.isBrowser() to conditionally run assertions.
hints: Cypress.isBrowser('chrome') returns true when running in Chrome
Cypress.isBrowser(['chrome', 'edge']) accepts an array
Use this for browser-specific feature tests

title: The Browser Oracle — skips test in specific browser
story: The Oracle instructs the test runner to skip a test when running in an incompatible browser.
objective: Use Cypress.isBrowser() to conditionally skip a test.
hints: Combine Cypress.isBrowser() with it.skip() for conditional skipping
if (Cypress.isBrowser('firefox')) return; inside the test body also works
This prevents false failures from browser-specific quirks

title: The Browser Oracle — reads isHeadless flag
story: CI runs Cypress headlessly. The Oracle checks Cypress.browser.isHeadless to change behaviour in CI vs local.
objective: Read Cypress.browser.isHeadless and use it in a conditional.
hints: Cypress.browser.isHeadless is true in 'cypress run' mode
It is false when running in 'cypress open' mode
Use it to skip slow visual assertions in CI

title: The Browser Oracle — reads browser family
story: Chrome, Chromium, and Edge share the same engine. The Oracle identifies the browser family to handle them uniformly.
objective: Use Cypress.browser.family to detect the browser rendering engine.
hints: Cypress.browser.family is 'chromium' for Chrome, Chromium, Edge
Cypress.browser.family is 'firefox' for Firefox
Cypress.browser.family is 'webkit' for WebKit-based browsers

title: The File Chooser
story: The File Chooser wields .selectFile() — the modern Cypress API for simulating file selection in <input type="file"> elements, replacing the old workarounds.
objective: Use .selectFile() to attach a file to an input element.
hints: .selectFile('cypress/fixtures/example.json') attaches a real fixture file
.selectFile() targets <input type="file"> elements
Cypress resolves the file path relative to the project root

title: The File Chooser — selects a virtual file

objective: Use .selectFile() with a virtual file defined by contents.

contents can be a string, Cypress.Buffer, or Blob

title: The File Chooser — drag and drop with selectFile
story: Some upload zones accept drag-and-drop. The Chooser uses the drag-drop action option to simulate this.
objective: Use .selectFile() with action: 'drag-drop' to simulate dropping a file.
hints: .selectFile(file, { action: 'drag-drop' }) triggers dragover and drop events
The target element must have drag event listeners
Useful for upload zones that do not use <input type="file">

title: The File Chooser — reads input files after selection
story: After selecting, the Chooser verifies the file was received by reading the input's files property.
objective: Assert on the files property of an input after .selectFile().
hints: After .selectFile(), use .then(input => input[0].files) to access the FileList
.its('files.length') asserts how many files are attached
The files property is a native FileList object

title: The Shadow Realm
story: Web components hide their internals in a Shadow DOM — invisible to normal selectors. The Shadow Realm wizard pierces through using .shadow() to reach the hidden elements.
objective: Use .shadow() to access elements inside a Shadow DOM.
hints: .shadow() pierces the shadow boundary of a host element
cy.get('my-component').shadow().find('button') queries inside the shadow root
Alternatively, enable experimentalShadowDomSupport in cypress.config.js

title: The Shadow Realm — finds nested shadow elements
story: Elements inside the shadow tree are found with .find() after crossing the shadow boundary.
objective: Chain .find() after .shadow() to locate a nested element.
hints:
cy.get('host').shadow().find('p') finds a

inside the shadow root
.find() works on shadow roots the same as on regular DOM trees
Nested shadow roots require chaining .shadow() multiple times

title: The Shadow Realm — clicks inside shadow DOM
story: Interactions inside shadow DOM work the same as in the regular DOM after crossing the boundary.
objective: Click an element inside a Shadow DOM using .shadow().find().click().
hints: cy.get('host').shadow().find('button').click() triggers events inside shadow DOM
Event propagation crosses shadow boundaries for most standard events
Shadow DOM clicks are subject to the same actionability checks

title: The Shadow Realm — includeShadowDom option
story: Enable includeShadowDom globally to make cy.get() pierce all shadow roots automatically.
objective: Use the includeShadowDom option to pierce shadow DOM without calling .shadow().
hints: cy.get('selector', { includeShadowDom: true }) pierces shadow roots globally
Set Cypress.config('includeShadowDom', true) to apply globally for a spec
This is useful when working with deeply nested web components

title: The Shadow Realm — asserts text inside shadow DOM
story: Text content inside shadow DOM is accessible with .should('have.text') after crossing the shadow boundary.
objective: Assert text content of an element inside Shadow DOM.
hints: .shadow().find('p').should('have.text', '...') asserts shadow element text
.shadow().find('p').invoke('text') extracts the text as a string
Chai text assertions work identically on shadow elements

title: The Focus Detective
story: Keyboard navigation and accessibility depend on focus management. The Focus Detective uses cy.focused() to get the currently focused element and assert it is the right one.
objective: Use cy.focused() to get the currently focused element.
hints: cy.focused() yields the element that currently has focus
If no element is focused, cy.focused() fails — use cy.focused({ log: false }) to suppress the error
Chain should() on cy.focused() to assert on the focused element
explanation:
**Tool:** Cypress
**Key APIs:** `cy.focused`, `focus`, `accessibility`, `keyboard`

Use cy.focused() to get the currently focused element.

Refer to the starter code comments for guidance on the required API calls. Use the 💡 Hint button above to reveal step-by-step hints if you get stuck.

title: The Focus Detective — asserts focused element type
story: The Detective checks not just which element is focused, but what kind of element it is.
objective: Assert the tag name of the focused element using cy.focused().
hints: cy.focused().invoke('prop', 'tagName') returns the tag name in uppercase
cy.focused().should('have.prop', 'tagName', 'INPUT') asserts the tag
Or: cy.focused().should('match', 'input') using CSS selector matching

Assert the tag name of the focused element using cy.focused().

title: The Focus Detective — tab key moves focus
story: The Tab key moves focus between interactive elements. The Detective verifies focus moves correctly after pressing Tab.
objective: Press Tab and use cy.focused() to verify focus moved to the next element.
hints: cy.focused().type('{tab}') or cy.get(el).type('{tab}') moves focus
After tabbing, cy.focused() yields the newly focused element
Test accessibility of keyboard navigation this way

title: The Focus Detective — blur removes focus
story: Calling .blur() removes focus from an element. The Detective verifies focus is no longer on the element after blurring.
objective: Use .blur() and verify cy.focused() no longer returns the blurred element.
hints: .blur() removes focus from the currently focused element
After blur, cy.focused() may return a different element or fail
Blur events trigger validation in many form libraries
explanation:

**Key APIs:** `.blur`, `cy.focused`, `focus`, `forms`

Use .blur() and verify cy.focused() no longer returns the blurred element.

title: The Focus Detective — have.focus assertion
story: The simplest focus assertion. The Detective uses .should('have.focus') directly on an element.
objective: Assert that a specific element has focus using should('have.focus').
hints: .should('have.focus') asserts the element is currently focused
.should('not.have.focus') asserts it is not focused
This is equivalent to document.activeElement === el

title: The Array Spreader
story: When a command yields an array, .spread() distributes each item as a separate argument to a callback. The Spreader handles multi-value yields with elegance.
objective: Use .spread() to destructure an array yielded by a Cypress command.
hints: .spread(fn) calls fn with each array item as a separate argument
Like .then() but spreads the array: .spread((a, b) => { })
Works on any command that yields an array

title: The Array Spreader — spreads cookie array
story: cy.getCookies() yields an array of cookies. The Spreader extracts each one by position.
objective: Use .spread() on cy.getCookies() to access individual cookies.
hints: cy.setCookie() then cy.getCookies() then .spread((c1) => { }) works
Each spread argument is a cookie object with name, value, domain, etc.
.spread() is preferable to .then((cookies) => cookies[0]) for clarity

title: The Array Spreader — spreads Promise.all results
story: Resolving multiple promises at once yields an array. The Spreader unpacks each resolved value.
objective: Use .spread() after resolving multiple Cypress.Promise values.
hints: cy.wrap(Promise.all([p1, p2])).spread((r1, r2) => { })
Each argument corresponds to a resolved promise
Useful when fetching multiple resources in parallel

title: The Array Spreader — spreads multiple elements
story: After getting multiple elements, the Spreader accesses each by position in the callback.
objective: Use .spread() on a multi-element result to access individual elements.
hints: cy.get('li').then($els => [...$els]).spread((el1, el2) => { }) spreads DOM elements
Convert jQuery collection to array first with [...$els]
Useful for comparing two specific elements side by side

title: The Array Spreader — spreads aliases
story: Multiple aliases can be collected into an array and spread. The Spreader accesses each aliased subject by name in the callback.
objective: Collect multiple aliases and spread them in a then callback.
hints: Store values using .as('name'), then retrieve with cy.get('@name')
To spread, collect all aliases first into an array
cy.get('@a') and cy.get('@b') return separate subjects — wrap them in an array

title: The Root Seeker
story: Every DOM tree has a root. The Root Seeker uses cy.root() to get the document root element, and .root() to get the root within a .within() scope.
objective: Use cy.root() to get the document root element.
hints: cy.root() yields the <html> element by default
Inside cy.within(), cy.root() yields the scoped element instead
Useful for resetting scope after deep traversals

title: The Root Seeker — root inside within()
story: Inside a .within() block, cy.root() returns the scoped element, not the document root. The Seeker uses this to escape the scope when needed.
objective: Call cy.root() inside a .within() block and see it returns the scoped element.
hints: Inside .within($el => { cy.root() }), cy.root() returns $el
This lets you get a reference to the within scope
It is the equivalent of "return to the top of this scope"

title: The Root Seeker — chains from root
story: Starting from the root ensures the selector is not accidentally scoped. The Seeker chains cy.root().find() to perform an absolute DOM query.
objective: Chain .find() from cy.root() to perform an absolute query.
hints: cy.root().find('selector') queries from the document root
This overrides any active .within() scope
Useful to break out of a scope without ending the within block

title: The Root Seeker — root vs document()
story: The Seeker compares cy.root() with cy.document() — both give access to the page top, but via different yields.
objective: Compare cy.root() and cy.document() to understand what each yields.
hints: cy.root() yields the <html> DOM element
cy.document() yields the document object (not a DOM element)
cy.document().its('documentElement') equals cy.root()

title: The Root Seeker — resets scope with root
story: Deep within a complex DOM, the Seeker resets to root to start fresh without ending the within block.
objective: Use cy.root() to reset context after navigating deep into the DOM.
hints: cy.root() inside .within() returns the scoped container, not the document
Outside .within(), cy.root() always yields <html>
Use cy.root().find() to restart a query from the top of scope

title: Your First Test
story: You have entered the Realm of Unit Tests. Every great tester starts with a single assertion. Write your first test to prove that 1 + 1 is indeed 2.
objective: Write a Jest test that calls expect(1 + 1).toBe(2) and passes.
hints: Use expect(value).toBe(expected) for strict equality.
expect(1 + 1).toBe(2) — wrap the expression inside expect().
A passing test exits with code 0.

title: Testing Objects with toEqual
story: A merchant hands you a mystical object. toBe will fail — it checks references, not contents. You need toEqual to compare object shapes.
objective: Write a test that compares two objects with the same shape using toEqual.
hints: toBe uses reference equality — it fails for objects with the same content but different references.
toEqual recursively checks every field.
expect(getUser()).toEqual({ name: 'Alice', age: 30 })

title: Truthiness Matchers
story: The Oracle speaks in truths and falsehoods. Master four matchers: toBeNull, toBeUndefined, toBeTruthy, and toBeFalsy.
objective: Write four tests — one each for toBeNull, toBeUndefined, toBeTruthy, and toBeFalsy.
hints: toBeNull() — only passes for null.
toBeUndefined() — only passes for undefined.
toBeTruthy() / toBeFalsy() — use JavaScript boolean coercion.

title: Strings and Arrays
story: The wizard's spell-book contains a list of ingredients. Test that a string matches a pattern and that an array contains the right item.
objective: Use toMatch to test a string and toContain to test an array.
hints: toMatch(regex) — checks if a string matches a regular expression.
toContain(item) — checks if an array includes the given item.
Both support .not to invert the assertion.

title: Testing Errors with toThrow
story: A cursed function throws an error when invoked. You must prove it throws — but wrap it in an arrow function or the curse will strike you first!
objective: Write a test that verifies a function throws using toThrow.
hints: ALWAYS wrap the function call in an arrow function: expect(() => fn()).toThrow()
toThrow() checks that any error is thrown.
toThrow('message') checks that the error message contains the string.

title: Async Testing with async/await
story: The Time Keeper's API is asynchronous. You must await the result before asserting on it — or the test will pass before the promise resolves.
objective: Write an async test that awaits a Promise and asserts on the resolved value.
hints: Mark the test callback as async.
Use await to unwrap the promise before asserting.
const result = await fetchTreasure(); then expect(result).toBe(...)
explanation:
`expect(value).toEqual(expected)` does a **deep equality** check — it compares object/array contents recursively, unlike `toBe` which uses `===`.

```
expect({ a: 1, b: [2, 3] }).toEqual({ a: 1, b: [2, 3] }); // passes
expect({ a: 1 }).toBe({ a: 1 });                           // FAILS (different object refs)
```

title: Mock Functions with jest.fn()
story: A spy has infiltrated the enemy ranks. Create a mock function, call it, and use Jest matchers to verify it was called with the right arguments.
objective: Create a jest.fn() mock, call it, and assert it was called with the correct arguments.
hints: jest.fn() creates a mock that tracks all calls.
toHaveBeenCalled() — passes if called at least once.
toHaveBeenCalledWith(arg1, arg2) — checks the exact arguments.
toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n) — checks the exact call count.

title: Setup and Teardown
story: The dungeon must be prepared before each battle and cleaned up after. Use beforeEach and afterEach to set up and tear down your test environment.
objective: Use beforeEach to initialize a value and afterEach to reset it. Write tests that depend on the setup.
hints: beforeEach runs before every test in the current describe scope.
afterEach runs after every test — use it to clean up.
Each test starts fresh because beforeEach re-initializes dungeon.

expect({ a: 1 }).toBe({ a: 1 });                           // FAILS (different object refs)

title: Mock Return Values
story: The oracle's prophecy changes with each question. Use mockReturnValueOnce to control what a mock returns on each call.
objective: Use mockReturnValueOnce to return different values on successive calls, then a default with mockReturnValue.
hints: mockReturnValueOnce(v) — returns v on the next call only.
mockReturnValue(v) — returns v as the default for all subsequent calls.
Chain them: oracle.mockReturnValueOnce('fire').mockReturnValueOnce('ice').mockReturnValue('unknown')

title: describe() and Grouping
story: A grand library organizes its tomes by subject. Use describe() to group related tests and give your test suite clarity and structure.
objective: Use describe() to group tests for a calculator's add and multiply functions.
hints: describe('add', () => { test(...); test(...); })
Each describe block creates a named scope for related tests.
You can nest describe blocks for further organization.

title: Greater Than
story: The hero's power must exceed the boss threshold. Prove it with numeric matchers.
objective: Use toBeGreaterThan and toBeGreaterThanOrEqual.
hints: toBeGreaterThan(n) — passes if value > n.
toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(n) — passes if value >= n.
Works with any numeric values.

title: Less Than
story: The dungeon temperature must stay below danger levels. Use less-than matchers.
objective: Use toBeLessThan and toBeLessThanOrEqual.
hints: toBeLessThan(n) — passes if value < n.
toBeLessThanOrEqual(n) — passes if value <= n.
Combine with not to assert ranges.

title: Floating Point
story: Magic potions blend imprecisely. toBe fails on 0.1+0.2. Use toBeCloseTo.
objective: Use toBeCloseTo for floating point comparison.
hints: toBeCloseTo(n) — checks equality within floating point precision.
Second argument is decimal places (default 2).
solution:
test('0.1 + 0.2 is close to 0.3',()=>{expect(0.1+0.2).toBeCloseTo(0.3);});
test('PI approximation',()=>{const pi=22/7;expect(pi).toBeCloseTo(3.14,2);});

title: Array and String Length
story: The guild roster must have exactly the right number of members. Use toHaveLength.
objective: Use toHaveLength on arrays and strings.
hints: toHaveLength(n) works on arrays, strings, and any object with a .length property.
expect([]).toHaveLength(0) — empty array.
Also works with .not to assert maximum length.

title: Object Properties
story: The wizard's spellbook must contain specific chapters. Use toHaveProperty.
objective: Use toHaveProperty to check object keys and nested paths.
hints: toHaveProperty(key) — checks key exists.
toHaveProperty(key, value) — checks key and value.
Use dot notation for nested paths: 'author.name'.

title: Partial Object Match
story: The treasure chest contains many items. You only care that it has the gold — use toMatchObject.
objective: Use toMatchObject to do partial object matching.
hints: toMatchObject checks that the object contains the expected properties.
Extra properties in the received object are ignored.
Use toEqual for exact matching with no extra properties.

title: Instance Checking
story: The potion must be a real Potion instance, not a fake. Use toBeInstanceOf.
objective: Use toBeInstanceOf to verify class instances.
hints: toBeInstanceOf(Class) — uses instanceof check.
All class instances are also instanceof Object.
Useful for checking Error types: toBeInstanceOf(TypeError).

title: expect.any()
story: The merchant's ID can be any number — you just need to confirm the type.
objective: Use expect.any() to assert value type without knowing the exact value.
hints: expect.any(Constructor) — matches any value created by that constructor.
Works inside toEqual, toMatchObject etc.
expect.any(Number), expect.any(String), expect.any(Function) are common.

title: expect.anything()
story: You don't care what the oracle returns — only that it returned something.
objective: Use expect.anything() to assert a value is not null or undefined.
hints: expect.anything() — matches anything except null and undefined.
Useful when the exact value is random but you need it to exist.
Combine with toMatchObject for partial object checks.

title: expect.arrayContaining()
story: The supply crate must include the essentials — you don't care about extra items.
objective: Use expect.arrayContaining to assert an array includes certain elements.
hints: expect.arrayContaining([...]) — matches if all listed items are present.
Order does not matter — it only checks membership.
Extra items in the array are ignored.

title: Return a Promise
story: The scout sends a Promise dispatch. Return it from your test so Jest awaits it.
objective: Return a Promise directly from a test (without async/await).
hints: Return the promise from the test — Jest waits for it.
If you forget to return, Jest finishes before the promise resolves.
Use .then() to assert on the resolved value.
solution:
function scoutReport(){return new Promise(r=>setTimeout(()=>r('all clear'),10));}
test('scout returns all clear',()=>{return scoutReport().then(msg=>expect(msg).toBe('all clear'));});

title: .resolves Matcher
story: The fortress gate should unlock. Use .resolves to unwrap the promise inline.
objective: Use .resolves to assert on a fulfilled Promise value.
hints: await expect(promise).resolves.toBe(value) — unwraps and asserts.
Must await or return the assertion.
Works with any matcher: .resolves.toEqual(), .resolves.toBeTruthy() etc.
solution:
function unlockGate(){return Promise.resolve('gate open');}
test('gate unlocks',async()=>{await expect(unlockGate()).resolves.toBe('gate open');});

title: .rejects Matcher
story: The forbidden spell must fail when cast. Use .rejects to verify the rejection.
objective: Use .rejects to assert a Promise rejects with the expected error.
hints: await expect(promise).rejects.toThrow(msg) — asserts rejection.
Must await or return the assertion or the test passes vacuously.
Can also use .rejects.toBeInstanceOf(Error).
solution:
function castForbiddenSpell(){return Promise.reject(new Error('spell forbidden'));}
test('forbidden spell rejects',async()=>{await expect(castForbiddenSpell()).rejects.toThrow('spell forbidden');});

title: expect.assertions()
story: A secret message arrives via callback. Declare the assertion count upfront to ensure it runs.
objective: Use expect.assertions(n) to guarantee async assertions execute.
hints: expect.assertions(1) — fails if not exactly 1 assertion runs.
Protects against tests passing when the callback never fires.
Place it at the top of the test.
solution:
function deliverMessage(cb){setTimeout(()=>cb(null,'secret scroll'),10);}
test('message is delivered',done=>{expect.assertions(1);deliverMessage((err,msg)=>{expect(msg).toBe('secret scroll');done();});});

title: Async Setup in beforeEach
story: Each battle requires async preparation — loading the arena. Use async beforeEach.
objective: Use async beforeEach to await setup before each test.
hints: Mark beforeEach as async and use await inside it.
Jest waits for the promise to resolve before running tests.
This pattern is common for DB connections or API calls in tests.

title: Multiple Awaits
story: The quest has multiple async checkpoints. Await each one in sequence.
objective: Write an async test that awaits multiple Promises in sequence.
hints: const s1 = await step1(); const s2 = await step2(s1); ...
Each await waits for the previous to complete.
Assert the final result with expect(s3).toBe(...)

title: Inspecting mock.calls
story: The spy recorded every conversation. Inspect mock.calls to see what was said.
objective: Access mock.calls to assert on individual call arguments.
hints: spy.mock.calls is an array of argument arrays.
spy.mock.calls[0] is the args of the first call.
spy.mock.calls[0][0] is the first arg of the first call.

title: Mock Return Values
story: The dice roller always returns what you program. Use mockReturnValue for consistent results.
objective: Use mockReturnValue to set a fixed return value.
hints: rollDice.mockReturnValue(6) — sets the default return value.
Every call returns 6 until changed.
mockReturnValueOnce for one-time values.
solution:
const rollDice=jest.fn().mockReturnValue(6);
test('dice always rolls 6',()=>{expect(rollDice()).toBe(6);expect(rollDice()).toBe(6);expect(rollDice()).toBe(6);});

title: mockResolvedValue
story: The async scout always reports success. Use mockResolvedValue for async mocks.
objective: Use mockResolvedValue to make a mock return a resolved Promise.
hints: fetchQuest.mockResolvedValue(data) — wraps data in Promise.resolve().
Equivalent to mockReturnValue(Promise.resolve(data)).
Use mockResolvedValueOnce for single-call async mocks.
solution:
const fetchQuest=jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({title:'Dragon Slayer',reward:500});
test('fetchQuest resolves with quest data',async()=>{const q=await fetchQuest();expect(q.title).toBe('Dragon Slayer');expect(q.reward).toBe(500);});

title: mockRejectedValue
story: The failing API always throws. Mock the rejection to test error handling.
objective: Use mockRejectedValue to make a mock return a rejected Promise.
hints: fetchVault.mockRejectedValue(new Error(...)) — wraps in Promise.reject().
Test with await expect(fn()).rejects.toThrow(...).
Use mockRejectedValueOnce for single-call rejection.
solution:
const fetchVault=jest.fn().mockRejectedValue(new Error('vault locked'));
test('fetchVault rejects',async()=>{await expect(fetchVault()).rejects.toThrow('vault locked');});

title: mockImplementation
story: The shape-shifter takes any form. Give it a real implementation with mockImplementation.
objective: Use mockImplementation to provide a custom function body.
hints: multiply.mockImplementation((a, b) => a * b)
Equivalent to jest.fn((a, b) => a * b).
Use mockImplementationOnce for a single call.
solution:
const multiply=jest.fn().mockImplementation((a,b)=>a*b);
test('multiplies correctly',()=>{expect(multiply(3,4)).toBe(12);expect(multiply(5,5)).toBe(25);});

title: toHaveBeenLastCalledWith
story: Only the final message to the king matters. Assert the last call arguments.
objective: Use toHaveBeenLastCalledWith to assert the arguments of the most recent call.
hints: toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(...args) — checks the last call's arguments.
Equivalent to checking mock.calls[mock.calls.length - 1].
Use toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(n, ...args) for a specific call number.
solution:
const sendMessage=jest.fn();sendMessage('attack north');sendMessage('retreat east');sendMessage('hold position');
test('last order was hold position',()=>{expect(sendMessage).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('hold position');});

title: toHaveBeenNthCalledWith
story: The courier delivered three scrolls. Assert exactly what was in the second delivery.
objective: Use toHaveBeenNthCalledWith to assert the arguments of a specific call.
hints: toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(n, ...args) — checks the nth call (1-indexed).
2nd call: toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2, ...).
Useful when testing that different calls had different arguments.
solution:
const deliver=jest.fn();deliver('scroll of fire');deliver('scroll of ice');deliver('scroll of lightning');
test('second delivery was ice',()=>{expect(deliver).toHaveBeenNthCalledWith(2,'scroll of ice');});

title: toHaveReturned
story: The function must complete without throwing and actually return something.
objective: Use toHaveReturned and toHaveReturnedWith to assert return values.
hints: toHaveReturned() — passes if the mock returned at least once (did not throw).
toHaveReturnedWith(value) — checks if any call returned that value.
toHaveLastReturnedWith(value) — checks the last return value.

title: jest.spyOn Basics
story: Spy on the blacksmith's hammer method without replacing it.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to spy on an existing method while keeping its implementation.
hints: jest.spyOn(obj, 'method') wraps the method and returns a mock.
The original implementation still runs.
Call spy.mockRestore() after the test to undo the spy.
solution:
const blacksmith={hammer(item){return`forged: ${item}`;}};
test('spy tracks calls',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(blacksmith,'hammer');const result=blacksmith.hammer('sword');expect(result).toBe('forged: sword');expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('sword');spy.mockRestore();});

title: Spy with mockReturnValue
story: Override the oracle's answer with a spy while still being able to restore it later.
objective: Use jest.spyOn + mockReturnValue to override a method's return value.
hints: jest.spyOn(obj, method).mockReturnValue(val) — spy + override return.
mockRestore() undoes the spy and restores the original implementation.
Without mockRestore, the override persists across tests.
solution:
const oracle={predict(){return Math.random()>0.5?'victory':'defeat';}};
test('oracle predicts victory',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(oracle,'predict').mockReturnValue('victory');expect(oracle.predict()).toBe('victory');spy.mockRestore();});

title: Spy on Math.random
story: Control fate itself — spy on Math.random to make dice deterministic.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to mock Math.random.
hints: jest.spyOn(Math, 'random') wraps the global Math.random.
mockReturnValue(0.5) makes it always return 0.5.
Always restore after the test.
solution:
function rollDice(){return Math.floor(Math.random()*6)+1;}
test('dice rolls 4',()=>{const spy=jest.spyOn(Math,'random').mockReturnValue(0.5);expect(rollDice()).toBe(4);spy.mockRestore();});

title: mockClear vs mockReset
story: After each skirmish, clear the battle records. Know the difference between clearing and resetting.
objective: Demonstrate the difference between mockClear (clears calls) and mockReset (clears calls + implementation).
hints: mockClear() — zeroes call count and instances, keeps implementation.
mockReset() — does everything mockClear does, plus removes implementation.
mockRestore() — restores original implementation (spyOn only).

title: beforeAll and afterAll
story: The expedition takes time to prepare and debrief. Use beforeAll/afterAll for one-time setup.
objective: Use beforeAll to set up once before all tests and afterAll to clean up.
hints: beforeAll runs once before all tests in the scope.
afterAll runs once after all tests in the scope.
Use for expensive setup like DB connections (unlike beforeEach).

title: Nested describe Scoping
story: The palace has outer halls and inner chambers. Each scope has its own setup.
objective: Use nested describe blocks to scope beforeEach differently per group.
hints: Inner beforeEach runs AFTER outer beforeEach.
Outer beforeEach sets 'outer hall', then inner sets 'inner chamber'.
Test outside describe uses only the outer beforeEach.

title: test.skip
story: The broken bridge must be skipped for now. Mark tests to skip without deleting them.
objective: Use test.skip to skip a test and keep it in the file.
hints: test.skip() or xtest() — marks the test as skipped (shown in output).
The skipped test will not run but appears in the report.
Use .only to run only specific tests during debugging.

const user = { id: 1, name: 'Aria', role: 'Mage', level: 99 };

```

`toMatchSnapshot()` captures the value on first run and compares on subsequent runs.

title: test.todo
story: The treasure map shows unexplored zones. Mark them with todo for future expeditions.
objective: Use test.todo to mark tests that need to be written.
hints: test.todo('description') — appears in output as a reminder.
No callback allowed — only the description string.
Useful for planning tests alongside implementation.

title: jest.useFakeTimers()
story: The time mage can freeze the clock. Replace real timers with fakes to test setTimeout.

hints: jest.useFakeTimers() replaces setTimeout, setInterval etc. with fakes.
jest.runAllTimers() fires all pending timers immediately.
Always call before the test code that uses timers.

title: advanceTimersByTime

objective: Use jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms) to advance the clock by a specific amount.
hints: jest.advanceTimersByTime(ms) moves the fake clock forward by ms milliseconds.
Only timers scheduled within that window will fire.
Call it multiple times to simulate time passing in steps.

title: setInterval with Fake Timers
story: The siege cannon fires every 500ms. Test the interval fires repeatedly.
objective: Use jest.useFakeTimers and advance time to test setInterval.
hints: setInterval fires every N ms — advancing 1500ms with 500ms interval = 3 fires.
jest.advanceTimersByTime fires all timers that fall within that window.
Check both call count and arguments.

title: runOnlyPendingTimers
story: Only fire the timers already scheduled — not new ones they trigger.
objective: Use jest.runOnlyPendingTimers() to fire only currently pending timers.
hints: runOnlyPendingTimers() fires currently queued timers but not new ones they schedule.
Call it again to fire the next batch.
Compare to runAllTimers which fires everything recursively.
explanation:
`expect(array).toContain(item)` checks that an array includes a value (using `===`).
`expect(array).toContainEqual(obj)` does deep equality for objects in arrays.

```
expect([1, 2, 3]).toContain(2);
expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: test.each — Array of Arrays
story: The alchemist needs to verify the same formula with many ingredients. Use test.each.
objective: Use test.each with an array of arrays for parameterized tests.
hints: test.each([[a,b,result], ...]) runs a test for each row.
%i in the name is replaced with the integer argument.
Parameters are passed in order to the test callback.
solution:
function add(a,b){return a+b;}
test.each([[1,2,3],[0,0,0],[-1,1,0],[100,200,300]])('add(%i,%i) equals %i',(a,b,expected)=>{expect(add(a,b)).toBe(expected);});
explanation:

```
expect([1, 2, 3]).toContain(2);
expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: test.each — Object Array
story: The merchant catalogue uses named fields. Use test.each with object rows.
objective: Use test.each with an array of objects for named test parameters.
hints: Object rows allow named parameters — use destructuring in callback.
$fieldName in the test name string is replaced with the value.
Much more readable than positional arrays for complex inputs.
solution:
function discount(p,pct){return p*(1-pct/100);}
test.each([{price:100,pct:10,expected:90},{price:200,pct:50,expected:100},{price:50,pct:0,expected:50}])('$price at $pct% discount is $expected',({price,pct,expected})=>{expect(discount(price,pct)).toBe(expected);});
explanation:

```

expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: describe.each
story: Multiple character classes need the same test suite. Use describe.each for full group parameterization.
objective: Use describe.each to run an entire describe block with different data.
hints: describe.each([...])(...) runs the full describe block for each row.
%s formats a string argument in the describe name.
Each row gets its own describe block with all its tests.
solution:
function getAttack(cls){const a={warrior:50,mage:80,rogue:60};return a[cls]||0;}
describe.each([['warrior',50],['mage',80],['rogue',60]])('%s class',(cls,exp)=>{test(`${cls} correct attack`,()=>{expect(getAttack(cls)).toBe(exp);});test(`${cls} attack positive`,()=>{expect(getAttack(cls)).toBeGreaterThan(0);});});
explanation:
`expect(array).toContain(item)` checks that an array includes a value (using `===`).

```
expect([1, 2, 3]).toContain(2);
expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: Edge Cases with test.each
story: Test the boundaries of the dungeon walls — 0, negative, max values.
objective: Use test.each to cover boundary/edge cases for a function.
hints: test.each is perfect for boundary testing.
Boundaries (min, max) and out-of-range values are classic edge cases.
Document expected values clearly in the test name format string.
solution:
function clamp(v,min,max){return Math.min(Math.max(v,min),max);}
test.each([[5,0,10,5],[-5,0,10,0],[15,0,10,10],[0,0,10,0],[10,0,10,10]])('clamp(%i,%i,%i)=%i',(v,min,max,exp)=>{expect(clamp(v,min,max)).toBe(exp);});
explanation:
`expect(array).toContain(item)` checks that an array includes a value (using `===`).
`expect(array).toContainEqual(obj)` does deep equality for objects in arrays.

```
expect([1, 2, 3]).toContain(2);
expect([{ name: 'Aria' }]).toContainEqual({ name: 'Aria' });
expect('Hello World').toContain('World'); // works on strings too
```

title: Testing Class Methods
story: The Knight class must prove it can attack and defend correctly.
objective: Write tests for a class with multiple methods.
hints: Use beforeEach to create a fresh instance for each test.
Test each method independently.
Test both happy path and edge cases (hp = 0).
solution:
class Knight{constructor(n,hp){this.name=n;this.hp=hp;}attack(){return 50;}defend(d){this.hp-=d;return this.hp;}isAlive(){return this.hp>0;}}
describe('Knight',()=>{let k;beforeEach(()=>{k=new Knight('Arthur',100);});test('attack',()=>{expect(k.attack()).toBe(50);});test('defend',()=>{expect(k.defend(30)).toBe(70);});test('isAlive',()=>{expect(k.isAlive()).toBe(true);});test('dead',()=>{k.hp=0;expect(k.isAlive()).toBe(false);});});

title: Spy on Class Method
story: Monitor the wizard's cast method without interrupting the spell.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to spy on a class instance method.
hints: jest.spyOn works on class instances, not just plain objects.
The real method still executes.
spy.mockRestore() removes the spy after the test.
solution:
class Wizard{cast(s){return`casting: ${s}`;}}
test('spy on cast',()=>{const w=new Wizard();const spy=jest.spyOn(w,'cast');w.cast('fireball');w.cast('ice bolt');expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('fireball');spy.mockRestore();});

title: mockImplementationOnce
story: The shape-shifter only transforms once, then reverts to normal form.
objective: Use mockImplementationOnce to return different results for the first call only.
hints: Chain .mockImplementationOnce(fn) before .mockImplementation(fn).
Once-values are consumed first, then the default kicks in.
You can chain multiple mockImplementationOnce for a sequence.

title: expect.objectContaining()
story: The hero's stats object has many fields. Only assert on the ones you care about.
objective: Use expect.objectContaining() to do partial object matching inside assertions.
hints: expect.objectContaining({...}) — passes if the object contains those keys with those values.
Extra keys in the received object are ignored.
Useful when objects have dynamic fields like timestamps.
solution:
function createHero(name){return{name,hp:100,mp:50,level:1,createdAt:new Date().toISOString()};}
test('hero has name and level',()=>{const h=createHero('Aragorn');expect(h).toEqual(expect.objectContaining({name:'Aragorn',level:1}));});

title: expect.stringContaining()
story: The battle log must mention the hero's name — you don't care about the exact message.
objective: Use expect.stringContaining() to do partial string matching.
hints: expect.stringContaining(str) — passes if the string includes str.
Works inside toEqual, toMatchObject etc.
Use expect.stringMatching(regex) for pattern matching.

title: toStrictEqual
story: The shapeshifter appears identical but its true type betrays it. Use toStrictEqual.
objective: Understand the difference between toEqual and toStrictEqual.
hints: toStrictEqual checks object types (class matters).
toStrictEqual distinguishes sparse arrays from arrays with undefined.
Use toEqual for general deep equality, toStrictEqual when class identity matters.

title: Testing Error Types
story: Different cursed artifacts throw different error types. Assert the exact error type.
objective: Use toThrow with a specific Error class and message.
hints: toThrow(TypeError) — checks instanceof TypeError.
toThrow(/pattern/) — checks message with regex.
Always wrap the call in () => to let Jest catch the throw.

title: Async Error with async/await
story: The vault API rejects bad keys asynchronously. Catch the async error.
objective: Use try/catch in an async test to handle rejected promises.
hints: Option 1: await expect(openVault('bad')).rejects.toThrow('invalid key')
Option 2: try { await openVault('bad') } catch(e) { expect(e.message).toContain('invalid key') }
Always pair with expect.assertions(1) when using try/catch.

title: Sharing State Safely
story: The guild register must be fresh for each test. Shared state between tests causes flaky failures.
objective: Use beforeEach to ensure each test starts with a clean state.
hints: Without beforeEach, tests share the same register instance.
State from one test pollutes the next (test order matters — bad).
Always use beforeEach to reset shared state.

title: Multiple Spies
story: Spy on both the king's messenger and his treasurer simultaneously.
objective: Use multiple jest.spyOn calls in one test and assert on both.
hints: Create multiple spies independently for different methods.
Restore each spy after the test to avoid cross-test pollution.
Order of assertions does not matter.
solution:
const court={sendMessage(m){return`sent: ${m}`;},transferGold(a){return`transferred: ${a}`;}};
test('king issues orders',()=>{const ms=jest.spyOn(court,'sendMessage');const gs=jest.spyOn(court,'transferGold');court.sendMessage('prepare for war');court.transferGold(1000);expect(ms).toHaveBeenCalledWith('prepare for war');expect(gs).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1000);ms.mockRestore();gs.mockRestore();});

title: Boss: The Mock Gauntlet
story: Face the Mock Gauntlet — combine jest.fn(), mockReturnValueOnce, spyOn, and assertion matchers in one epic test.
objective: Combine multiple mocking techniques in a single test suite.
hints: Use mockReturnValueOnce for first call, mockReturnValue for fallback.
jest.spyOn preserves the original — check return value AND call.
Restore spies after each test.

title: Boss: Async + Mocks
story: The final dungeon combines async fetching with mocked dependencies. Conquer both.
objective: Write an async test that uses a mocked async dependency.
hints: mockResolvedValue on a spy makes it return a resolved promise.
await the function under test.
The spy intercepts the DB call — getItemName gets the mocked data.

title: Your First Snapshot
story: The wizard wants to freeze time and compare past vs present. Snapshot testing saves the day.
objective: Use toMatchSnapshot() to capture and compare output.
hints: toMatchSnapshot() saves output on first run and compares on subsequent runs.
If snapshot changes intentionally, run jest --updateSnapshot.
Works with strings, objects, arrays.
solution:
function greet(n){return`Hello, ${n}!`;}
test('greet snapshot',()=>{expect(greet('World')).toMatchSnapshot();});

title: Object Snapshot
story: The artifact details must be preserved exactly. Snapshot the whole object.
objective: Snapshot a plain object to detect unexpected changes.
hints: toMatchSnapshot() deep-serialises objects.
Any key added or changed will fail the test.
Update with --updateSnapshot when changes are intentional.
solution:
function getArtifact(){return{id:1,name:'Sword of Truth',damage:50};}
test('artifact snapshot',()=>{expect(getArtifact()).toMatchSnapshot();});

title: Inline Snapshot
story: The scribe wants the expected value written right in the scroll. Use inline snapshots.
objective: Use toMatchInlineSnapshot() with the expected string inline.
hints: toMatchInlineSnapshot(`"OK"`) — value goes directly in the test file.
Jest auto-fills the argument on first run if you leave it empty.
Backtick template literal wraps the expected serialised string.
solution:
function status(c){return c===200?'OK':'Error';}
test('status inline snapshot',()=>{expect(status(200)).toMatchInlineSnapshot(`"OK"`);});

title: not.toBe
story: Two heroes must be different people. Assert they are NOT the same reference.
objective: Use .not.toBe() to assert two objects are not the same reference.
hints: .not inverts any matcher.
.toBe uses Object.is (reference equality).
{} !== {} even if contents match — that's what not.toBe checks.
solution:
const h1={name:'Alice'},h2={name:'Alice'};
test('different references',()=>{expect(h1).not.toBe(h2);});

title: not.toEqual
story: Two spells must have different effects. Deep-compare and assert they differ.
objective: Use .not.toEqual() to assert two objects have different values.
hints: .not.toEqual does deep inequality check.
.toEqual and .not.toEqual are mirrors.
{damage:10} and {damage:20} are not deeply equal.
solution:
const s1={damage:10},s2={damage:20};
test('spells differ',()=>{expect(s1).not.toEqual(s2);});

title: not.toContain
story: The banned item must not appear in the hero's inventory.
objective: Use .not.toContain() to assert an array does not include a value.
hints: .not.toContain checks item is absent from array.
Also works on strings: expect(str).not.toContain(substr).
Uses strict equality for array item checks.
solution:
const inv=['sword','shield','potion'];
test('no cursed item',()=>{expect(inv).not.toContain('cursed ring');});

title: not.toBeNull and not.toBeUndefined
story: The quest result must actually exist — it must be neither null nor undefined.
objective: Use .not.toBeNull() and .not.toBeUndefined() together.
hints: .not.toBeNull() — value is not null.
.not.toBeUndefined() — value is not undefined.
toBeDefined() is the short form for not.toBeUndefined.
solution:
function findQuest(id){return id===1?{name:'Slay the Dragon'}:null;}
test('quest exists',()=>{const r=findQuest(1);expect(r).not.toBeNull();expect(r).not.toBeUndefined();});

title: toBeDefined
story: The merchant must have a price set before selling. Verify the price is defined.
objective: Use toBeDefined() to verify a value is not undefined.
hints: toBeDefined() — not undefined.
toBeUndefined() — is undefined.
These are opposites of each other.

title: toHaveBeenCalledTimes
story: The blacksmith must be called exactly twice — once to forge, once to temper.
objective: Use toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n) to verify exact call count.
hints: toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n) — mock was called exactly n times.
Works only on jest.fn() or jest.spyOn targets.
Use toHaveBeenCalled() if you only care it was called at least once.
solution: test('forge called twice',()=>{const forge=jest.fn();forge('sword');forge('shield');expect(forge).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);});
explanation:
`screen.getByRole` finds elements by their ARIA role — the most accessible and resilient query: ``` screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }) // screen.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Login' }) //

title: Clearing Mock State

objective: Use mockClear() to reset call history but keep return value.
hints: mockClear() resets calls, instances, results — NOT implementation.
mockReset() also removes implementation/return values.

objective: Use mockReset() to clear state AND remove implementation.
hints: mockReset() clears everything including return values.

Use in afterEach to ensure clean state per test.
solution: test('mock reset',()=>{const p=jest.fn().mockReturnValue(100);p();p.mockReset();expect(p).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0);expect(p()).toBeUndefined();});

title: toThrowError with Message

hints: toThrow(string) checks the error message contains that string.
toThrow(ErrorClass) checks the instance type.

solution:
function openVault(k){if(k!=='secret')throw new Error('Invalid key');return'open';}
test('wrong key throws message',()=>{expect(()=>openVault('wrong')).toThrow('Invalid key');});

title: toThrow with Regex

objective: Use toThrow(/regex/) to pattern-match error messages.
hints: toThrow(/pattern/) tests message against regex.
The regex only needs to match a substring.
Use ^ and $ anchors for exact matches.
solution:
function cast(s){if(!s)throw new Error('Spell cannot be empty');return'casting';}
test('empty spell error',()=>{expect(()=>cast('')).toThrow(/cannot be empty/);});

title: Custom Error Classes

title: toHaveLength on String

title: toHaveLength on Array

objective: Use toHaveLength() on an array.

title: toContainEqual

title: Async Error with try/catch

const healer={heal(a){return`Healed ${a} HP`;}};

solution:

test('delivery confirmed',(done)=>{deliverMessage((r)=>{expect(r).toBe('message delivered');done();});});

title: Callback Error Handling

hints: done(err) fails the test with the given error.

solution:
function riskyDelivery(s,cb){setTimeout(()=>{if(s)cb(null,'delivered');else cb(new Error('Failed'),null);},10);}

title: Testing an Event Emitter

solution:
class Bell{constructor(){this._listeners={};}on(e,fn){this._listeners[e]=this._listeners[e]||[];this._listeners[e].push(fn);}emit(e,...a){(this._listeners[e]||[]).forEach(fn=>fn(...a));}}
test('bell rings',()=>{const b=new Bell();const ring=jest.fn();b.on('ring',ring);b.emit('ring','loud');expect(ring).toHaveBeenCalledWith('loud');expect(ring).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);});

title: Testing a Generator

hints: gen.next() returns { value, done }.

solution:
function* dungeonRooms(){yield'entrance';yield'hallway';yield'boss room';}
test('dungeon rooms',()=>{const gen=dungeonRooms();expect(gen.next().value).toBe('entrance');expect(gen.next().value).toBe('hallway');expect(gen.next().value).toBe('boss room');expect(gen.next().done).toBe(true);});

title: Testing Closures
story: A counter closes over its count. Each call increments it. Test the closure.
objective: Test a closure that maintains private state.
hints: The closure captures count in the enclosing scope.
10 + 2 increments - 1 decrement = 11.
Each makeCounter() call creates independent state.
solution:
function makeCounter(start=0){let count=start;return{increment(){count++;},decrement(){count--;},value(){return count;}};}
test('counter',()=>{const c=makeCounter(10);c.increment();c.increment();c.decrement();expect(c.value()).toBe(11);});

title: Testing Higher-Order Functions
story: The spell composer wraps functions for extra power. Test the higher-order function.
objective: Test a function that accepts and returns functions.
hints: The HOF wraps the original function.
log is a jest.fn to spy on calls.
result should be the return of the original function.
solution:
function withLogging(fn,log){return function(...args){log(`calling with ${args}`);return fn(...args);};}
test('with logging',()=>{const log=jest.fn();const add=(a,b)=>a+b;const loggedAdd=withLogging(add,log);const result=loggedAdd(3,4);expect(result).toBe(7);expect(log).toHaveBeenCalledWith('calling with 3,4');});

title: Memoization Testing
story: The oracle remembers previous answers to avoid recalculating. Test memoization.
objective: Test a memoize function that caches results.
hints: The underlying function should only be called once per unique input.
jest.fn tracks how many times it was called.
Cache hit = no call to expensive.
solution:
function memoize(fn){const cache={};return function(n){if(n in cache)return cache[n];cache[n]=fn(n);return cache[n];};}
test('memoize caches results',()=>{const expensive=jest.fn(n=>n*2);const memo=memoize(expensive);memo(5);memo(5);memo(5);expect(expensive).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);expect(memo(5)).toBe(10);});

function countVisits(log){const c=new Map();for(const h of log){c.set(h,(c.get(h)||0)+1);}return c;}
test('visit counts',()=>{const c=countVisits(['Alice','Bob','Alice','Alice']);expect(c.get('Alice')).toBe(3);expect(c.get('Bob')).toBe(1);expect(c.has('Carol')).toBe(false);});

test('retry succeeds on third try',async()=>{const fn=jest.fn().mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('fail 1')).mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('fail 2')).mockResolvedValueOnce('success');const result=await retry(fn,3);expect(result).toBe('success');expect(fn).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);});

function withLogging(fn,logger){return function(...args){logger.log(`called with ${JSON.stringify(args)}`);const result=fn(...args);logger.log(`returned ${result}`);return result;};}

story: The dungeon records commands for undo/redo. Test the command history.

title: LRU Cache
story: The dungeon caches only the most recent 3 rooms. Test LRU eviction.
objective: Test an LRU cache implementation with get and set.
hints: Map preserves insertion order — oldest is first.

solution:
class LRUCache{constructor(c){this._cap=c;this._cache=new Map();}get(k){if(!this._cache.has(k))return -1;const v=this._cache.get(k);this._cache.delete(k);this._cache.set(k,v);return v;}set(k,v){if(this._cache.has(k))this._cache.delete(k);else if(this._cache.size>=this._cap){this._cache.delete(this._cache.keys().next().value);}this._cache.set(k,v);}}
test('lru eviction',()=>{const lru=new LRUCache(2);lru.set(1,'a');lru.set(2,'b');lru.get(1);lru.set(3,'c');expect(lru.get(2)).toBe(-1);expect(lru.get(1)).toBe('a');expect(lru.get(3)).toBe('c');});

title: Boss: Algorithms Gauntlet
story: 210 levels complete. The algorithms gauntlet — data structures, memoization, and mocks.
objective: Combine LRU cache, binary search, and mock logging in one suite.
hints: First search(5) is a miss — binary search runs.

solution:
class SearchCache{constructor(c,l){this._lru=new Map();this._cap=c;this._log=l;}search(a,t){if(this._lru.has(t)){this._log.hit(t);return this._lru.get(t);}let lo=0,hi=a.length-1,result=-1;while(lo<=hi){const mid=Math.floor((lo+hi)/2);if(a[mid]===t){result=mid;break;}if(a[mid]<t)lo=mid+1;else hi=mid-1;}this._log.miss(t);if(this._lru.size>=this._cap)this._lru.delete(this._lru.keys().next().value);this._lru.set(t,result);return result;}}
test('cache miss then hit',()=>{const logger={hit:jest.fn(),miss:jest.fn()};const sc=new SearchCache(2,logger);const arr=[1,3,5,7,9];const r1=sc.search(arr,5);const r2=sc.search(arr,5);expect(r1).toBe(2);expect(r2).toBe(2);expect(logger.miss).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);expect(logger.hit).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);});

function makeCircuitBreaker(t){let failures=0,open=false;return async function call(fn){if(open)throw new Error('Circuit open');try{const r=await fn();failures=0;return r;}catch(e){failures++;if(failures>=t)open=true;throw e;}};}

solution:
function compose(...mws){return function(ctx,next){let index=-1;function dispatch(i){if(i<=index)throw new Error('next() called multiple times');index=i;const fn=mws[i]||next;if(!fn)return;fn(ctx,()=>dispatch(i+1));}dispatch(0);}}

hints: clearAllMocks = reset calls/instances/results only.
resetAllMocks = clearAllMocks + remove all mock implementations.
restoreAllMocks = resetAllMocks + restore original spied functions.

title: Spy on Date.now()
story: Freeze the dungeon clock at a specific moment. Spy on Date.now().
objective: Use jest.spyOn to control Date.now() return value.
hints: jest.spyOn(Date, 'now') spies on the static method.
mockReturnValue fixes the timestamp.
After mockRestore, Date.now() returns real time again.

title: Spy on Math.random()
story: The dungeon dice is rigged. Control Math.random() with a spy.
objective: Use jest.spyOn on Math.random and verify functions that use it.
hints: Math.random() returns [0, 1). 0.5 * 6 = 3.0, floor = 3, +1 = 4.
0 → minimum roll of 1; just below 1 → maximum of 6.
Always restore after spying on global methods.

title: Mock a Callback Dependency
story: The dungeon event handler is injected as a callback. Test it gets called correctly.
objective: Test a function that accepts a callback by passing a jest.fn() as the argument.
hints: Pass jest.fn() as the callback arguments.
Verify call count and arguments for each branch.
not.toHaveBeenCalled() asserts the callback was NOT triggered.

title: Mock Chained Methods
story: The dungeon query builder chains methods. Mock the full chain.
objective: Create a mock that supports method chaining.
hints: mockReturnThis() returns the mock object itself, enabling chaining.
The final .execute() returns the actual data.
Verify each chained method was called with the right args.

title: Spy on Class Constructor
story: Track every hero instantiated by the factory. Spy on the class constructor.
objective: Use jest.spyOn to track instantiation via a factory method.
hints: Spy on the factory method, not the class itself.
The real Hero instances are still created.
Verify each create() call with the right arguments.

title: Verify No Unexpected Calls
story: The healer must never call the attack method. Verify mock silence.
objective: Assert that specific mock methods were NOT called during a flow.
hints: not.toHaveBeenCalled() is just as important as toHaveBeenCalled().
Verify both what WAS called and what WASN'T.
This prevents accidental side effects in production.

title: mockReturnValue on Spy After Call
story: The oracle spoke the truth once. Now make it lie forever after.
objective: Call a spy once with real impl, then override it with mockReturnValue.
hints: Before mockReturnValue, the real impl runs.
After mockReturnValue, the mock takes over permanently.
Total calls = 1 real + 2 mocked = 3.

title: Capture Arguments with mock.calls
story: Extract and verify the exact arguments from every mock invocation.
objective: Use mock.calls to capture and assert on all invocation arguments.
hints: mock.calls is an array of arrays: [[arg1], [arg1], ...].
call[0] is the first argument (the object in this case).
Map over mock.calls to extract specific fields.

title: Mock Throwing Errors
story: The cursed sword always throws when swung. Make the mock throw.
objective: Use mockImplementation to make a mock throw an error.
hints: mockImplementation(() => { throw ... }) makes the mock throw.
toThrow checks the error is raised.
Combine with mockReturnValue for throw-then-succeed patterns.

title: Boss: Mock Mastery Gauntlet
story: 250 levels conquered. The Mock Mastery Gauntlet — every mock technique in one battle.
objective: Combine jest.fn(), spyOn, mockImplementation, mock.calls, and async mocks.
hints: Success: info called twice (before and after), error never called.
Failure: info once (before), error once, then throws.
gateway.process receives the amount and default currency.

title: Mock Event Listener
story: The dungeon door emits events. Mock addEventListener and verify registration.
objective: Mock an event listener registration and verify the handler was attached.
hints: Mock the DOM-like element with jest.fn() for addEventListener.
toHaveBeenCalledWith(event, handler) checks both arguments.
Useful for testing code that wires up events.

title: Mock setTimeout Callback
story: The delayed message must fire after one second. Verify the callback via fake timers.
objective: Combine jest.useFakeTimers with a mock callback to verify delayed execution.
hints: Before advancing time, the callback has not run yet.
jest.advanceTimersByTime(1000) triggers the 1000ms timeout.
Verify both call count and the argument.

title: Spy on Promise.resolve
story: Track every promise resolution in the dungeon network layer.
objective: Spy on a method that returns a promise and verify async behavior.
hints: mockResolvedValueOnce overrides the async result for one call.
Await the result and assert on the data.
spy.mockRestore() restores the real async implementation.

title: Mock Return Object with Methods
story: The dungeon service returns an object with methods. Mock the whole thing.
objective: Mock a function that returns an object with its own mockable methods.
hints: Mock the factory function with mockReturnValue pointing to the mock object.
The mock object has its own jest.fn() methods.
Verify each method call independently.

title: Boss: Full Mock Architecture
story: 255 levels. The ultimate mock architecture — a full service layer with injected mocks.
objective: Test a multi-layer service with database, cache, logger, and event bus — all mocked.
hints: register: all four deps are called.
get with cache hit: only cache.get and logger.debug are called.
expect.objectContaining handles the dynamic id from Date.now().
